provenance.note: The statements are authored; every figure is measured here from the pinned source, and the fourth convention's giver is read from priors/pos-eng.json's provenance. nomos.js derives each convention's standing from its own giver or builder; a standing written here would not be believed.

conventions.says: In a cased script a capital in the middle of a sentence marks a name.
conventions.scope: cased scripts (Latin, Cyrillic, Greek) written in standard orthography

witnesses.says: of the PROPN tokens that are not first in their sentence, the share written with a capital
of the other tokens that are not first in their sentence, the share written with a capital
of the capitalised tokens that are not first in their sentence, the share that are PROPN

witnesses: khora native/the-fold/language-context.js header: standard prose, SMS, Singlish and IRC capitalise 2-13% of non-initial tokens, and capitals mostly mark names
conventions.basis: extracted — measured from the received ground's own PROPN tags; a nomination with its witnesses, not a licence
departs: a caseless script has no capital
an all-lower-case text (SMS, OCR) keeps none: the case-free floor of surfaces.js stands in

conventions.says: The first word of a sentence is capitalised by position, so a sentence-initial capital is no evidence of a name.
conventions.scope: cased scripts; holds where the sentence cut finds the sentence

witnesses.says: of the capitalised sentence-initial tokens, the share that are PROPN

conventions.basis: extracted — measured from the received ground's own PROPN tags; a nomination with its witnesses, not a licence
departs: a name that only ever opens a sentence is invisible to the capital tier: khora organs/hypergraph.js "the referent bar" confirms it by a real pronoun binding (not passed to the reader by read-core.mjs)

conventions.says: A sentence ends with a terminal mark, so the capital after one opens a sentence.
conventions.scope: running prose; the sentence cut (khora adapters/text/spans.js) reads by it

witnesses.says: of the gold sentences, the share whose last token is no terminal mark (headings, bylines, captions, list items)

conventions.basis: extracted — measured from the received ground's own sentence segmentation; a nomination with its witnesses, not a licence
departs: a heading, byline or list item run into the next sentence puts that sentence's capital in the middle of a cut: the lone capital of "Grab", "Well", "Okay" after one, which the next convention answers

conventions.says: How a form is used, tag by tag, is attested by a human-annotated treebank; a capital the text cannot test is weighed against that use.
conventions.scope: English; a single-word candidate the text never writes lower-case
conventions.giver: Universal Dependencies — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UniversalDependencies/UD_English-EWT/master/en_ewt-ud-train.conllu (train split), human-annotated gold treebank

witnesses.reproduces: 16654 forms recounted from en_ewt-ud-train.conllu, 0 differ, 0 missing

witnesses: khora native/adapters/text/wordclass.js::classifyWord is the repo's lens over it; nothing is re-read
the ground the cast is scored on (UD_English-GUM) is a different corpus
conventions.basis: received — the rule's giver is a named ground (UD_English-EWT); silent for a form the treebank has not seen, which then stays a being
departs: the prior is keyed on the case-folded form, so a form that is both a name and a function word (a twin, derived from the prior's own PROPN and closed-class base rates: on pos-eng.json "us" and "may"; "Will" is not one) has counts that mostly describe its lower-case twin: it is returned undecided with the tied set {name, function word}, not decided by counts, unless the text separates the readings by the form heading a capitalised run (khora eval/referents/PREREG-TWIN.md)
no pos prior, a language other than English, or a language with no filed stem: the giver is silent and the capital tier is what it was
